🛑 Critical Engineering Evaluation: Is the Dataset Sufficient?

The honest, objective answer is NO — not yet for an autonomous, production-ready AI camera recognition system.
While 91 curated landmark sites with 541 multi-angle photos is excellent for an initial MVP pitch to hackathon judges, deploying a real-world camera companion app across Indian monuments reveals four major structural deficits.

The 4 Core Sufficiency Gaps & Why They Matter for SIH26204:

1. The Macro Coverage Gap (The Breadth Problem)

India has 3,696 Centrally Protected Monuments under ASI, over 4,000 State Protected Monuments, and 15.6 Lakh built heritage structures / antiquities registered under the National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities (NMMA). A dataset of 91 entities only covers ~0.005% of documented Indian built heritage. If a tourist opens the camera app at Gohilwad Timbo (Amreli), Dada Harir Stepwell (Ahmedabad), or Khambhalida Buddhist Caves (Rajkot), a 91-entity model returns a complete zero-shot hallucination or out-of-vocabulary error.

2. Real Tourist Camera Conditions vs. Canonical Wikimedia Photos (The Vision Robustness Gap)

Postcard-style Wikimedia Commons photos are taken by professional photographers on tripods under pristine golden hour lighting with zero crowd obstruction. Real tourists hold mobile phones at a 45-degree angle from the ground, in 42°C harsh midday Indian sun (50,000 lux glare), with 50 people blocking the lower half of the frame, motion blur from walking, and low-budget smartphone sensor noise. In computer vision research (e.g. Google Landmarks Dataset v2), training a robust vision model requires 100 to 500+ diverse tourist-shot images per landmark class covering all angles, seasons, and lighting conditions.

3. The Micro-Artifact / Museum Depth Gap

When a tourist enters the National Museum Delhi or Baroda Museum, they do not point their camera at the building exterior — they point it at individual display cases containing Indus Valley seals, Kushan gold coins, Chola bronzes, Mughal daggers, and Rajput miniature paintings. The National Museum alone houses over 200,000 artifacts; Salar Jung Museum houses 46,000. 12 sample artifacts in a dataset cannot support a functioning museum companion without specialized museum API integrations (like Museum of India portal).

4. The Multi-Tier Production Architecture (How We Solved It Today)

To turn this into a winning Hackathon submission, we have structured the repository into four functional production tiers:
• Tier 1 (Micro-Curated RAG Showcase): 91 landmark sites with 541 multi-angle working photos, scannable architectural features, and curatorial RAG narratives for jury demonstration.
• Tier 2 (Exhaustive Gujarat State Atlas): All 203 Centrally Protected ASI monuments in Gujarat with district breakdown, GPS coordinates, and direct links to Commons photo archives.
• Tier 3 (All-India ASI National Registry): Complete census of all 3,936 Centrally Protected Monuments across all 28 states and UTs with downloadable CSV/JSON.
• Tier 4 (Edge Inference Pipeline): GPS Geofencing pre-filter (reducing 3,936 candidates to <10 within 25km radius) + SigLIP/DINOv2 contrastive visual retrieval + GLDv2 data augmentation spec.
